legal_design_anchors.gdpr_article_11: Do not acquire, maintain or process additional identifying information solely to identify a data subject when identification is not required for the research purpose; where the controller can demonstrate it cannot identify the data subject, rights that require identification are handled in accordance with Article 11 unless the data subject provides additional information enabling identification.
legal_design_anchors.gdpr_article_12: The controller must provide transparent information and facilitate exercise of data-subject rights through the approved privacy contact and procedure.
legal_design_anchors.gdpr_article_18: Where restriction applies, the record must not continue through ordinary analytical processing while the restriction is active. The reference design therefore permits storage for rights handling but excludes a held record from analytical export.
legal_design_anchors.gdpr_article_21: Where processing relies on legitimate interests and a data subject objects, processing must stop while the controller assesses the objection unless a lawful continuation ground is established. The reference design therefore applies a fail-closed analytical hold during review.

identification_policy.technical_receipt: The submit route returns an opaque response_id. It is not derived from name, email, IP, device, CRM or employer identity. If retained by the respondent, it may be used to locate the corresponding research-only record without creating an identity lookup table.
identification_policy.lost_receipt_rule: If the controller cannot otherwise identify the record, it must not create a new identity-linkage mechanism solely to satisfy lookup. The Article 11 position and any additional information voluntarily provided by the data subject must be assessed by the approved controller procedure.

request_channel.rule: No public collection until the determined controller publishes an operational privacy contact and request-handling route.

research_store_operations.lookup: Locate only by opaque response_id in the isolated research store; do not search CRM, optional-contact records, IP logs, user-agent logs or device data.
research_store_operations.access: Return only the respondent-level analytical record associated with the receipt after the controller applies the approved request-authentication procedure; do not expose internal idempotency digests or other respondents.
research_store_operations.rectification: If applicable and technically safe, replace only the validated preset analytical values for that response_id and regenerate integrity metadata; otherwise document why rectification cannot be performed without undermining integrity and offer erasure/re-submission where appropriate.
research_store_operations.erasure: Delete the analytical row, any active analysis hold and its idempotency receipt atomically from live research storage. To prevent a delayed transport retry from recreating data that the respondent already erased, the reference adapter retains only the opaque response_id as a non-analytical replay-suppression marker. The reference adapter has no default retention and refuses an erasure that would create this marker unless a finite UTC not-after boundary is explicitly injected. At or after that boundary, replay markers are purged automatically before replay checks. The marker contains no questionnaire answers, body digest, raw Idempotency-Key, identity, contact, IP, user-agent, device, CRM or employer data. The live PROD boundary must be separately bounded and approved in the retention schedule before collection. Residual backups follow the validated non-renewing backup rotation in the retention schedule.
research_store_operations.restriction_or_objection: The reference adapter supports a receipt-keyed analysis hold. A restricted or objected record remains available for the controller's rights review but is excluded from analytical export while the hold is active. Any live implementation must preserve this fail-closed behavior and apply the controller-approved legal outcome.

rights_case_logging.allowed: minimum case metadata needed to demonstrate handling, decision, dates and outcome
forbidden: copying questionnaire answers into the rights-case log
adding CRM/customer identifiers to analytical records
using a rights request to build an identity-to-response registry
copying rights-case narrative into the research analysis-hold table

backup_and_deletion.rule: Live erasure must be evidenced by row/object counts and a timestamped deletion receipt. The minimal replay-suppression marker is not analytical evidence, must never enter NF06/export and requires its own controller-approved bounded lifecycle. The reference adapter proves the fail-closed shape by requiring an explicit finite boundary and providing deterministic expiry/purge behavior; it does not select the PROD duration. Provider backups may retain residual encrypted copies only for the validated pre-existing rotation and must not silently restore deleted or held records into active analysis.

required_before_prod: privacy notice updated with the final rights procedure
processor/subprocessor and provider logging/backup/deletion facts frozen
production research-only adapter supports receipt lookup, bounded analysis holds, atomic erasure and anti-replay suppression so erased data cannot be recreated by a delayed retry
controller approves the minimum necessary replay-marker retention bound and the live binding injects a finite UTC not-after boundary with automatic purge/deletion evidence
restriction/objection handling is operationally approved for the live adapter

provider-bound TEST TWIN rights smoke proves held records cannot enter analytical/NF06 export, erased records cannot be resurrected before the approved replay boundary, and replay markers expire at the approved boundary
procedure approval reference and SHA-256 are frozen in the PROD activation manifest

test_twin.rule: Rights-flow tests use synthetic engineering fixtures only and cannot be cited as respondent evidence.
